stream_runtime.scope: real LUKS/systemd/QEMU lifecycle with synthetic data; nested TCG is NOT an isolation guarantee
stream_runtime.workload: session gateway grant, private token delivery and network isolation
checks: PASS: general unlock without an API key leaves gateway services and VM stopped
PASS: encrypted external SOCKS profile is selected before the key starts the gateway
PASS: reselecting the current key records the RAM choice without restarting its gateway or Tor bootstrap
PASS: A receives a RAM token privately; real broker authenticates it, rejects bad tokens and reports the synthetic provider's offline probe
PASS: compiled OpenCode uses the production launcher and local token; the broker accepts its payload and returns the disabled-provider error
PASS: compiled adapter receives SSE through the real session VM, private grant, supervisor and gateway broker
PASS: active streaming blocks a transport change without interrupting or replacing its gateway
PASS: controller revocation closes the provider TLS stream and the adapter reports failure while QEMU and its LUKS mapping are still open
PASS: revocation precedes vault closure and removes broker access even while the old guest remains running
PASS: explicit key selection replaces the gateway VM; the real compiled adapter sends the alternate key only through the broker
PASS: session QEMU death revokes its active upstream stream through the pidfd observer before explicit volume closure
PASS: B rejects A's token; SIGKILL of its QEMU automatically revokes the broker and closes the matching pidfd while the volume remains interlocked until explicit close
PASS: reopened A gets a third token; owner death destroys its gateway access and explicit closure removes both LUKS mappings
PASS: unlock restores the persisted SOCKS route and credentials without reading or changing Tor state
PASS: a frozen host owner cannot acknowledge revoke; closure instead destroys the gateway before releasing the session volume
PASS: normal QEMU exit also revokes automatically; repeated opens bind fresh process handles and global lock closes both volumes
PASS: fragmented private requests expire despite continued progress; the owner destroys its gateway VM and leaves storage state explicit
PASS: runtime regular files contain none of the synthetic provider keys or session tokens after closure

host_runtime.scope: real LUKS/systemd/QEMU lifecycle with synthetic data; nested TCG is NOT an isolation guarantee
host_runtime.workload: systemd service crash/recovery with real manager and VM
checks: PASS: interrupted general filesystem formatting retains an unpublished file and retry never overwrites it
PASS: recovery latches before a busy operation lock and only verified closure clears it
PASS: systemd waits for controller readiness and runs the confined manager as UID 1000
PASS: fragmented controller frames and secrets expire despite continued progress; the same service accepts the next valid request
PASS: outer disk exhaustion cannot publish a partial general volume; explicit cleanup permits retry
PASS: trusted setup confirms discard, recreates a complete general volume and protects existing archives
PASS: trusted manager saves a hidden API key only in the root-owned encrypted profile; status and manager UID cannot retrieve it
PASS: trusted network menu saves hidden proxy credentials only in the root-owned encrypted profile; offline policy refuses external proxies
PASS: temporary transport stays in RAM; saved selection restores it; unknown fields, aliases and corrupt profiles never trigger a fallback
PASS: full-disk transport update preserves the prior profile; retry replaces the interrupted private staging file
PASS: invalid keys and staging aliases are rejected; an interrupted private staging file permits an atomic retry
PASS: legacy key is read without migration; ENOSPC preserves it and retry publishes the versioned archive before deleting the legacy file
PASS: full-disk replacement preserves the archive; published archives take precedence over leftover legacy secrets and malformed archives fail closed
PASS: key persists across lock/unlock; removal requires confirmation and cancellation preserves it
PASS: trusted manager adds and renames a second hidden key, saves its default and selects another key only in RAM
PASS: active chat blocks persistent, temporary and saved-profile transport changes
PASS: key picker chooses the opening credential; an active session blocks key mutations and identity changes
PASS: removing the selected key never rotates to the remaining account; explicit default and selection restore access
PASS: read-only transport choices use RAM, clear on lock and leave the entire encrypted image byte-identical
PASS: read-only profile exposes key metadata and permits RAM selection, rejects all key mutations and pending deletion, and remains byte-identical
PASS: interrupted session formatting survives restart, cannot open, and is discarded only after confirmation
PASS: disk exhaustion is explicit, preserves existing archives and permits reopening after pending cleanup
PASS: SIGKILL of manager powers down the VM and closes both LUKS mappings before restarting
PASS: SIGKILL of controller stops its dependent manager and recovers before both restart
PASS: unresponsive VM leaves recovery latched and rejects every new opening
PASS: recovery survives restart; cancelled force-stop preserves VM; explicit confirmation closes both volumes
PASS: controller stop drains dependent services and leaves no active VM or open volume
PASS: synthetic passwords, API keys and proxy credentials never appear on the managed console

limits: Outer x86 Debian host uses KVM; nested gateway and session use explicit laboratory TCG. Not a production session-KVM or physical USB isolation proof.
Provider/proxy uses synthetic credentials and a laboratory-only additional TLS root. Production broker trust, endpoint and TLS verification remain unchanged.
No outer NIC and no Internet traffic. This run has no packet capture; the separate 21-case matrix supplies transport/firewall capture evidence, not a complete trace of these host sessions.

Tests an authenticated external SOCKS route, key selection, revocation and persistence. Does not test a host Tor-to-SOCKS transition, real provider, real Tor provider flow, or global OS shutdown during an active stream.
Fixture verifies its host executable hash and the gateway image manifest. External variant does not read a runtime broker hash through the gateway console.

Disk canary scan covers synthetic passwords, keys and proxy credentials; it is not a fresh scan for every prompt, response or possible filesystem residue. Runtime scan covers regular files beneath /run after closure.
Generic tool proxy, approval UI, expiring permissions and persistent rules remain incomplete. The later policy evaluator commit is not covered by this run.
Transfer services, full ephemeral guest, signed live-image provisioning and physical hardware/fault verification remain separate release gates.
